content_preview.title: Valve-Sponsored Collabora Effort Ports Mesa's Open-Source RADV Vulkan Driver to Windows, Already Running Counter-Strike 2
content_preview.summary: Collabora, funded by Valve, has ported an early version of the open-source RADV Vulkan driver from Linux to Windows, reaching the point where it can launch Counter-Strike 2.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Valve is sponsoring an experimental effort by open-source consultancy Collabora to bring RADV — the open-source Mesa Vulkan driver for AMD graphics cards — to Microsoft Windows, according to [Collabora](https://www.collabora.com/news-and-blog/news-and-events/cracking-windows-open-porting-radv-to-win32.html) and [Phoronix](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Valve-Sponsors-RADV-Windows). The early-stage port has already reached a working milestone: it can launch the game Counter-Strike 2, ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis) at 883 words, within the 400-1200 word News range. Technical material (WDDM2, D3DKMT, DXGI, MSVC enum handling) is explained accessibly without oversimplifying.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three source snapshots directly from sources/2026-08/valve-sponsored-collabora-effort-ports-mesas-open-source-radv-vulkan-driver-to-windows-already-running-counter-strike-2/ (source-0.html.gz = Collabora, source-1.html.gz = Phoronix, source-2.html.gz = Linuxiac). All three confirm the core event: Valve-sponsored Collabora port of RADV to Windows, running Counter-Strike 2. collabora.com is not yet in config/source_allowlist.txt (flagged by the automated check as a warning), but it is the primary source — the engineering company's own official blog, written by the engineer (Louis-Francis Ratté-Boulianne) who did the work — and is credible on its own merits; phoronix.com and linuxiac.com are both already allowlisted.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Verified character-for-character against the raw snapshots: (1) Faith Ekstrand's 2024 proof-of-concept lineage — Collabora's post confirms she 'first explored the feasibility of running RADV on Windows and presented her findings at XDC 2024,' used the wddm2-pdd-re tool, and got a rotating 3D model displayed; Linuxiac explicitly confirms she 'demonstrated at XDC 2024 that RADV could communicate with AMD's proprietary Windows kernel-mode driver.' (2) Counter-Strike 2 launching via `-vulkan` — confirmed verbatim in Collabora ('Anyone can try it by switching the renderer with the -vulkan argument') and Linuxiac ('the port can launch Counter-Strike 2 by starting the game with the -vulkan command-line argument'). (3) 'Not production-ready' caveats — no full Vulkan conformance (Collabora: 'still not conformant'; Linuxiac: 'does not yet pass the full Vulkan conformance test suite'), CPU-only presentation (Collabora: 'RADV currently only supports the slower CPU path for presentation'), and the reverse-engineered/undocumented kernel interface (Collabora's D3DKMT/private-driver-data discussion) all check out. RX 7900 XT vs. RX 7800 XT hardware generations, the MSVC enum-signedness bug, and the '3x' zero-copy performance estimate also verified verbatim against Collabora's post. FINDING: the article presents the sentence 'a unified codebase, simplified debugging capabilities, accelerated bug fixes, and community pathways for contribution' in quotation marks attributed to Collabora. The actual source text reads: 'a shared codebase across platforms, easier debugging and experimentation, faster turnaround on fixes, and a path for the community (e.g., game developers) to report problems or contribute improvements that benefit everyone regardless of operating system.' This is a paraphrase, not a verbatim quote — every phrase has been reworded while kept inside quotation marks. The two Phoronix/Collabora quotes about the 'stable, documented interface... or a shim library' fork in the road were checked and are accurate verbatim (matching, with the Collabora one combining two adjacent bullet-list items without ellipsis, which is a truncation style issue, not a wording error).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Appropriately hedges the project's significance in the Analysis section as sponsorship-driven and non-production rather than overselling it.

concerns: One quotation attributed to Collabora ('a unified codebase, simplified debugging capabilities, accelerated bug fixes, and community pathways for contribution') is a paraphrase of the source's actual wording, not a verbatim quote, despite being presented in quotation marks. The underlying claim (the port offers these benefits) is substantively accurate and supported by the source; only the specific wording inside the quote marks is fabricated.

editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, accurate reporting on a new topic, undermined by a single fabricated-verbatim quotation (the true underlying claim is accurate, but the quote marks around reworded text are dishonest to the source). This is a textbook single recoverable issue, not a pattern of fabrication, and does not touch the headline/summary/lead — APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS with a corrections record covering the misquote.
